Series::bitwise_or¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series::bitwise_or(const Series& rhs) const -> Series
Series& Series::bitwise_or_(const Series& rhs) const

What It Does¶

bitwise_or() combines two operands bit by bit and keeps any bit that is set in either operand.

If bitwise_and() asks “which bits survive in both?”, bitwise_or() asks “which bits appear anywhere across the pair?”

Parameters¶

rhs (const Series&)

The right-hand operand. It must broadcast with self and use an integer or boolean dtype.

Returns¶

Series A new Series containing the bitwise union of the two operands.

In-Place Form¶

bitwise_or_() is the in-place sibling of bitwise_or(): it computes the same result and writes it back into self directly — mutating it (and any other handle sharing the same storage) instead of allocating a new Series — then returns a reference to self.

Despite being declared const at the call site — a quirk of how this method’s wrapper is generated, not a promise that self is left unchanged — bitwise_or_() genuinely mutates the series it’s called on.

auto x = pluss::make_series({6, 12}, pluss::ScalarType::Int64);
auto y = pluss::make_series({3, 10}, pluss::ScalarType::Int64);

x.bitwise_or_(y);
std::cout << x;

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[2], strides=[1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[7, 14]

Examples¶

Example 1. Integer bitwise union keeps every 1 bit that appears on either side.

auto left = pluss::make_series({1, 6, 12, 10}, pluss::ScalarType::Int32);
auto right = pluss::make_series({3, 10, 5, 12}, pluss::ScalarType::Int32);

std::cout << left.bitwise_or(right);

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[4], strides=[1], dtype=int32, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[3, 14, 13, 14]

Example 2. The same dtype restriction applies to the whole bitwise family.

try {
  auto a = pluss::make_series({1.0, 2.0});
  auto b = pluss::make_series({1.0, 0.0});
  std::cout << a.bitwise_or(b);
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  std::string msg = e.what();
  std::cout << msg.substr(0, msg.find('\n'));
}

Output¶

bitwise: dtype must be integer/bool

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • This is not arithmetic addition.

  • Floating-point operands fail fast.

  • Bitwise methods operate on stored bits, so the result is best read as a bit pattern first and a numeric magnitude second.

Summary¶

Use bitwise_or() when you need the bitwise union of two inputs.

See Also¶

  • Series::bitwise_and: keeps only overlapping bits.

  • Series::bitwise_xor: keeps differing bits only.

  • Series::logical_or: truth-value union rather than raw bit union.
